plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-ollama-web

English | [日本語](README.ja.md) | [中文](README.zh.md)

Ollama Cloud web search and optional web fetch provider for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH), with a Web UI settings card. One npm package provides both the host backend and the browser card. Search uses Ollama; `web_fetch` stays on DSH's built-in HTTP provider unless you explicitly enable the optional Ollama fetch provider.

[![Support via Buy Me a Coffee](https://img.shields.io/badge/Buy%20Me%20a%20Coffee-FFDD00?style=flat-square&logo=buymeacoffee&logoColor=black)](https://buymeacoffee.com/explorrrr)

- Search endpoint defaults to `https://ollama.com/api/web_search`
- Optional fetch endpoint defaults to `https://ollama.com/api/web_fetch`; off by default
- Configure the API key in the card (write-only) or via `OLLAMA_API_KEY`
- Update checks, install, and opt-in auto-update are included
- Default `web_fetch` remains the credential-free DSH HTTP provider

## Requirements

- DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 (peer `>=0.2.1-rc.1 <0.3.0`), tested on this version
- DSH 0.3.x is not supported yet (planned for 3.0); see [docs/COMPATIBILITY.md](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md)
- Node.js >= 20.3
- An Ollama Cloud API key from <https://ollama.com/settings/keys>

## Install

One package provides the `web_search` backend, the optional fetch provider and the settings card. Install it once.

1. Add the package.

   ```bash
   dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-ollama-web@2.4.0
   ```

   Replace `desktop` with your profile name if needed. You can also use **Plugins -> Add plugin** in the Web UI. npm: [dsh-ollama-web](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-ollama-web)

2. Pin the search provider in `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`.

   ```yaml
   - id: web
     config:
       searchProvider: ollama
       fetchProvider: http

   # Only if the built-in DeepSeek search provider is mounted.
   - id: web-search-deepseek
     disabled: true
   ```

   `fetchProvider: http` keeps `web_fetch` on DSH's built-in HTTP provider.

### Optional Ollama fetch provider

To use Ollama for `web_fetch`, enable the provider **and** pin it. Both entries are required:

```yaml
- id: web
  config:
    searchProvider: ollama
    fetchProvider: ollama

- id: ollama-web
  config:
    enableFetchProvider: true
```

`web` replaces its whole config, so keep `searchProvider: ollama` when you change `fetchProvider`. With only `enableFetchProvider: true`, `web_fetch` reports `WEB_PROVIDER_AMBIGUOUS` because both the HTTP and Ollama fetch providers are usable. With only `fetchProvider: ollama`, it reports `WEB_PROVIDER_CONFIGURED_UNAVAILABLE` because the Ollama provider is disabled. You can also enable the provider from the settings card, but the `web.fetchProvider: ollama` pin still belongs in the profile patch.

Ollama does not expose the target page's HTTP status or final redirect URL. A successful Ollama fetch is reported to DSH as `HTTP 200` for the requested URL; title, main content and links are folded into the text result. Keep `fetchProvider: http` when target status fidelity or DSH's local SSRF boundary matters.

### Upgrading from 1.x

2.0.0 merges the former `dsh-ollama-web-client` package into `dsh-ollama-web`. Remove the old package before installing 2.4.0:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove dsh-ollama-web-client
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-ollama-web@2.4.0
```

The 1.x updater checks both old packages and only auto-installs the current major. Because 2.0.0 is not published as a new `dsh-ollama-web-client`, it will not move you to 2.0.0; the upgrade is manual. In the desktop app, remove the `dsh-ollama-web-client` bundle in **Plugins**, then install `dsh-ollama-web@2.4.0`. Leaving the old client installed can register the settings card twice and is not supported.

## Configure

### API key

Enter it in the settings card (**Plugins -> `dsh-ollama-web` -> `ollama-web` -> Configure**), or set `OLLAMA_API_KEY` in the environment that launches DSH. The card is write-only: leaving the key blank keeps the current key, and a saved key is never shown again.

### Settings

| Field | Default | Constraint |
|---|---|---|
| `baseURL` | `https://ollama.com` | HTTPS only; no userinfo/query/fragment |
| `apiKeyEnv` | `OLLAMA_API_KEY` | `^OLLAMA_[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` |
| `searchPath` | `/api/web_search` | Absolute path under the baseURL path, same origin |
| `maxResults` | `5` | 1-10 |
| `snippetMax` | `2000` | 1-10000 characters |
| `maxQueryChars` | `2048` | 1-8192 characters |
| `searchTimeoutMs` | `30000` | 1000-120000 ms |
| `maxResponseBytes` | `2097152` | 65536-10485760 bytes |
| `fetchPath` | `/api/web_fetch` | Absolute path under the baseURL path, same origin |
| `fetchTimeoutMs` | `30000` | 1000-120000 ms |
| `fetchMaxChars` | `100000` | 1-200000 characters |
| `enableFetchProvider` | `false` | Live boolean; requires `web.fetchProvider: ollama` |
| `apiKey` | unset | Secret; prefer the card or `OLLAMA_API_KEY` |

`apiKeyEnv` accepts only `OLLAMA_*` names. Other environment variables and credential references are rejected before a request is made.

## Usage

Ask the model to search, then check that results come from Ollama. The search request body contains only the query and `max_results`; the API key is sent in the `Authorization: Bearer` header. The default endpoint is `https://ollama.com/api/web_search`.

When the optional fetch provider is enabled and pinned, `web_fetch` sends only `{ "url": "..." }` to `https://ollama.com/api/web_fetch` with the same Bearer key. Ollama returns `title`, main-content `content` and `links`; this plugin folds them into a text result and caps it at `fetchMaxChars`. The request URL is returned as the result URL and the status is always `200` on success, because Ollama does not expose the target status or final redirect URL.

### If the settings card does not appear

1. Confirm `dsh-ollama-web` is installed and its bundle is enabled.
2. Refresh the Web page.
3. Check that the package name is `dsh-ollama-web` and the row is `ollama-web` (the card key is `dsh-ollama-web#ollama-web`).
4. Fall back to the patch configuration above; the host works without the card.

## Updates

**Plugins -> `dsh-ollama-web` -> Configure** (or the bundle detail page) shows an Updates section. As of 2.2.0, the bundle detail page also shows the support card. Opening this screen performs a fresh check when the last successful check is older than five minutes; **Check for updates** always checks immediately. Use **Check for updates** / **Install update**, then restart DSH (quit and reopen the desktop app) to load the new version.

- **Check:** the host reads the npm registry (fallback: npmmirror) and honours the profile's pnpm `minimumReleaseAge` only when it is explicitly set. Unset, unreadable, invalid or `0` means no age wait. A release newer than a configured age is shown as waiting instead of being installed.
- **Compatibility:** the updater compares the release's `engines.dsh` with the running DSH version (`DSH_CLIENT_VERSION` or `DSH_APP_VERSION`). A known-incompatible release is blocked; if compatibility cannot be verified, auto-update pauses while the manual Install button remains available.
- **Install:** downloads one tarball, verifies the npm SHA-512 integrity and the archive, then atomically replaces the installed package. A failed swap rolls the previous copy back.
- **Auto-update (opt-in):** off by default. When enabled, the host checks every 6 hours and installs a newer **same-major** release that supports the running DSH. Major updates require the explicit button.
- **Caveats:** a `link:` or external-directory development install is never modified. DSH 0.2.1 has no third-party update API, so the updater replaces installed files directly. The profile's `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` still record the previous version; reinstall through **Plugins** (or the CLI) if you want those records updated.

See [docs/UPDATES.md](docs/UPDATES.md) for details.

## Security

- Host plugins run in-process, outside the workspace sandbox. Review plugins before installing and pin versions.
- Search is HTTPS-only, refuses redirects, caps response/query/snippet sizes

plugins.description: Expose the running DeepSeek Harness Web GUI's authenticated URL as an agent tool (gui_auth_url), so browser automation can open the GUI instead of failing with 401. Install: dsh plugin --profile web add github:NingYuanLee/dsh-gui-auth-url
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-gui-auth-url

[![CI](https://github.com/NingYuanLee/dsh-gui-auth-url/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/NingYuanLee/dsh-gui-auth-url/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![dsh](https://img.shields.io/badge/dsh-%3E%3D0.2.1--rc.2%20%3C0.3.0--0-6f42c1)](package.json)
[![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/NingYuanLee/dsh-gui-auth-url?style=social)](https://github.com/NingYuanLee/dsh-gui-auth-url/stargazers)

> Third-party community plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). Not an official DeepSeek product. MIT licensed.

English | [中文](README-zh.md) | [Español](README-es.md) | [Português](README-pt.md) | [हिन्दी](README-hi.md)

Expose the running DeepSeek Harness Web GUI's **authenticated URL** as an agent tool, so browser automation and scripts can open the GUI instead of hitting `401 dsh web authentication required`.

## The problem

`dsh --profile web` mints a random launch token per process and prints it once:

```text
dsh web: http://127.0.0.1:3080/?token=...
```

`GET /?token=...` verifies the token, sets a signed cookie bound to host:port, and redirects to `/`. Opening the bare address returns:

```text
401 dsh web authentication required; reopen the URL printed by dsh web.
```

The Desktop edition starts its own Host process on a random port and never prints that line, so any external browser or automation tool opening `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` always gets 401. There is no `--no-browser-auth` switch today.

## How it works

The plugin runs inside the Host process and asks the official public API `connection.authenticatedUrl(baseUrl)` — the same call `dsh web` uses to build the URL it prints — then returns the result as a tool result.

It never reads the cookie-signing secret in `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml` and never mints a cookie itself, so the URL is a genuine first-party session bound to this process.

Base URL resolution prefers `webApp.getAdvertisedUrl()` (respects `--public-url` and mounts), then `webServer.getOrigin()`, then protocol plus loopback port. Every call re-reads the live value, so random Desktop ports and restarted tokens need no cache. The token is attached only when that base is absolute `http` or `https`, has no username or password, and — unless the plugin config sets `allowPublic: true` — names a loopback host (`127.0.0.0/8`, `localhost`, or `::1`). The returned URL must be that same origin and carry exactly one `token`. An unacceptable base is refused before `authenticatedUrl` is called, and the error text never includes the URL.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:NingYuanLee/dsh-gui-auth-url
```

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so `dsh plugin add` writes the bundle into the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` automatically. Restart DeepSeek Harness and the tool appears.

Local checkout instead:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/NingYuanLee/dsh-gui-auth-url.git
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-gui-auth-url
```

The package is published on npm as `dsh-gui-auth-url`. GitHub is the source repository.

Upgrading from the old name `dsh-gui-session` (0.1.x): the package name, Cordis row id and tool name all changed, so reinstall once:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <name> remove dsh-gui-session
dsh plugin --profile <name> add github:NingYuanLee/dsh-gui-auth-url
```

## Usage

The plugin registers one tool, `gui_auth_url`, with no parameters. It returns:

```json
{
  "url": "http://127.0.0.1:3080/?token=...",
  "origin": "http://127.0.0.1:3080",
  "protocol": "http:",
  "host": "127.0.0.1",
  "port": "3080",
  "secure": false
}
```

The model sees the `url` text; the other fields are available to programmatic callers. Hand the URL to `navigate_page`, `curl`, or any HTTP client to enter the GUI.

Typical use: while debugging DeepSeek Harness itself, let the agent open the live GUI with chrome-devtools-mcp and verify layout, interaction and RPC for real instead of guessing from code.

## Security

- The returned URL contains **this process's launch token**. It is a credential equivalent to a signed-in session and only works while the Host process is alive.
- Do not write it to logs, commit it, or paste it into chats. Regenerate by calling the tool again; a restart invalidates it.
- A successful call still places the token in the session transcript and in later model requests. "Do not write it to logs" does not stop the host from storing the tool result. That is a wider audience than the one line `dsh web` prints in a terminal.
- The plugin does not read `.credentials.yaml` and does not mint cookies.
- Non-loopback URLs (`--public-url`, a LAN address, or `0.0.0.0`) are refused unless the plugin config is exactly `allowPublic: true`. That flag trusts the advertised host.
- It is unrelated to [Discussion #8678](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/8678) (reading the signing secret inside a sandbox to forge cookies): this plugin never touches that secret.

## Compatibility

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| dsh | `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0-0` |
| Node | `>=22.19.0` |
| Verified on | dsh `0.2.1-rc.2`, Windows x64, desktop and web profiles |
| Web combination | needs the `connection` service; a profile without a Web GUI reports a clear error |

Display metadata (`locale/*.json` plus the exported `./icon`) makes the Plugins page and Settings show a proper title, description and artwork instead of the raw package id. The plugin does not require a build step: it ships plain ESM JavaScript.

## Troubleshooting

**The tool does not appear after install.** Check that the profile's `package.json` lists `dsh-gui-auth-url` in `dsh.profile.bundles`. `dsh plugin add` normally writes it, but a failed install can leave only the dependency:

```json
{
  "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["@deepseek-ai/dsh-base", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app", "dsh-gui-auth-url"] } }
}
```

Restart DeepSeek Harness, then confirm with `dsh --profile <name> --dump-config` and look for the `gui-auth-url` row.

**Installation rejected because of a version mismatch.** DSH checks `engines.dsh` (or dsh peer ranges) at install time. If your host is outside the declared range, grant the exact-version exemption, reinstall, and revoke it once a compatible release exists:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> version-exemptions
dsh plugin --profile <profile> allow-version dsh-gui-auth-url@0.2.1 --dsh-version <runtime> --accept-risk
dsh plugin --profile <profile> revoke-version dsh-gui-auth-url@0.2.1
```

**`EPERM: rename ... node_modules\dsh-gui-auth-url_tmp_*` on Windows.** Stop the DSH process using that profile, delete the stale `node_modules\dsh-gui-auth-url` directory, and retry. A running process locks the directory.

**"This profile serves no Web GUI".** The plugin only returns a URL when the profile mounts `webApp` or `webServer` plus `connection`. Headless-style profiles have no GUI to open.

**"refusing to attach the launch token to a non-loopback host".** The advertised URL is not loopback. The token is not returned. To allow that host, set this entry in the profile patch. A later patch replaces the whole `config` object, so keep any other keys you need in that same object:

```yaml
- id: gui-auth-url
  config:
    allowPublic: true
```

Leave `allowPublic` unset on a Desktop loopback profile. The flag trusts whatever `webApp.getAdvertisedUrl()` returns.

## Development

```bash
node --test test/*.test.js          # unit + manifest compliance tests
node --check src/index.js && node --check src/auth-url.js
npm run check:pack                  # verifies the published tarball contents
```

```text
src/auth-url.js    pure helpers: base URL resolution + Host session call (unit-tested)
src/index.js       Cordis plugin entry: registers the gui_auth_url tool
locale/            display metadata (en, zh, es, pt, hi)
test/              node:test suites, including packaging invariants
scripts/           tarball check used by prepublishOnly and CI
```

The plugin only registers a tool; `ctx.tools.register` returns the disposer that Cordis owns, so unloading or hot-reloading the pl

plugins.description: 复杂项目模式 preset for DeepSeek Harness (dsh): the standard tool stack plus a four-document policy, current-state-only docs, a no-unrequested-push rule, careful coding, and plain-language reporting.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-complex-project-preset

**An agent preset for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): the full standard tool stack, plus the discipline to think before it types.**

> 中文版: [README.zh.md](README.zh.md)

The whole preset lives in [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml): it inserts one `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` row into the profile and registers a preset with the id `complex-project`. The package ships **configuration only** — no host code, no browser UI — so there is very little that an upgrade can break.

---

## Why

The standard preset gets work done, but it will not hold a line on its own: diffs creep, project docs turn into changelogs, and code goes up before you said so.

This preset writes four rules into the persona prompt, so every session starts with them already in force:

| Rule | In one line |
| --- | --- |
| Four documents | A project keeps at most four docs: intro, decisions, change log, current state & next steps |
| Current state only | No AI edit history, no superseded decisions, no leftover "stage 1–5" wording |
| Commit/push red line | No `git commit`, `git push`, or PR until you explicitly say so |
| Careful coding + plain language | Restate the goal and the done-criteria first, make surgical diffs, lead reports with the conclusion |

## What's inside

The tool stack matches the standard preset — bash/pwsh chosen per platform, file read/write and search, tasks and background jobs, skills, plan mode, compaction, subagents and workflows, web fetch, the TODO tool, present. What differs is the persona prompt and the documentation rules:

- `persona` — the four-document policy, current-state-only docs, the commit/push red line, the careful-coding rules, and plain-language reporting;
- `agent-instructions` — still loads your global `AGENTS.md` (64 KB cap);
- `planning` / `compaction` / `delegation` — same groups and isolation settings as standard;
- `tool-plugin-manager` — disabled, so the agent cannot rewrite its own plugin tree.

> ⚠️ The persona block deliberately sets **no `suffix`**. DSH registers only `provider` and `model` as prompt variables; any other `{{name}}` throws during prompt assembly and the whole turn fails before a single request is sent. The working directory is injected by the runtime context already, so declaring it here is redundant as well as fatal.

## Install

```sh
# from npm (recommended — prebuilt install, no build approval)
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-complex-project-preset

# or from the repository / a local directory
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/sueqet/dsh-complex-project-preset
dsh plugin --profile web add link:<local-dir>
```

**Restart the profile** (run `dsh web` again, or restart the desktop app) — a preset is a row in the profile composition, not a runtime hot-load.

Uninstall: `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-complex-project-preset`

### Conflicts with a hand-rolled copy

If your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` already declares `- id: preset-complex-project` by hand, installing this package registers the same preset twice and DSH reports `Duplicate agent preset: complex-project`. To switch over:

1. delete that `- id: preset-complex-project ...` block from your `cordis.patch.yml`;
2. `dsh plugin --profile <name> add dsh-complex-project-preset`;
3. restart the profile.

Only one package should provide `complex-project` at a time.

### Version requirement

Requires **DSH ≥ 0.1.7-rc.2** (the preset registry `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset-registry` joins the base composition there) and **Node.js ≥ 22.19.0**. Verified on DSH 0.1.7-rc.2 and on the desktop build 0.2.1-rc.2.

The Node floor is the harness's own rather than this package's: DSH compositions call `process.getBuiltinModule`, which Node ships from 22.3 onwards. This package is a manifest plus one YAML patch — no host code, no browser code, no install-time scripts — so it never loads JavaScript of its own, and the floor only mirrors where DSH can run at all.

## Verify

After a restart, open the mode picker for a new session: **复杂项目模式** (order 2, right after the standard preset) should be listed. Start a session with it and ask about the project's current state — the answer should talk in terms of the four documents rather than freeform.

From the CLI you can also inspect the composed tree:

```sh
dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep -A3 preset-complex-project
```

## Develop

```sh
npm test          # checks manifest + cordis.patch.yml consistency, including !!js parsing
npm pack --dry-run
```

`tools/smoke.mjs` verifies that `dsh.bundle.patch` points at a file that exists, that `repository` points back at this repo, that every required preset field is present, that child row ids are unique, and that the persona prompt is neither truncated nor carrying a stray `suffix`. It parses the patch with the harness's own `loadOverlayPatches` when available, so `!!js` expressions behave exactly as they do at boot.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE) © 2026 sueqet

plugins.description: bioRxiv preprint search, version/status and export tools for DeepSeek Harness (dsh). Zero runtime dependencies.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-biorxiv

bioRxiv preprint search, version/publication status and export tools for DeepSeek Harness (dsh). Zero runtime dependencies.

> Status: `0.1.0-alpha` — functional core, not a 1.0 release. Relevance evaluation is provisional; do not treat it as peer-reviewed evidence.

## Tools

- `biorxiv_search` — search bioRxiv preprints by topic, optional date window and field. Default `minScore=3` filters low-confidence text matches; set `minScore=0` for higher recall.
- `biorxiv_paper` — DOI lookup: latest version, publication DOI/journal, retraction flag when available.
- `biorxiv_latest` — latest preprints by date window and optional category.
- `biorxiv_export` — export search results or one DOI as JSON, Markdown, CSV or BibTeX.
- `biorxiv_digest` — structured markdown digest (extractive by default; optional opt-in Chinese summaries; no automatic delivery).

All tools return a stable envelope:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {},
  "error": { "code": "", "message": "", "retryable": false, "hint": "" },
  "meta": { "requestId": "...", "elapsedMs": 12, "cached": false, "source": ["europepmc"], "warnings": [] }
}
```

On failure `ok` is `false`, `data` is `{}`, and `error.code` is one of `E-001`–`E-010`.

## Install (one command)

```bash
dsh plugin --profile headless add github:TYEclipse/dsh-biorxiv#v0.1.0-alpha.20
```

Replace `headless` with the target profile. `dsh plugin add` is a pnpm forwarder: a `--profile` is required, and `pnpm` must be on `PATH`.

Build from source instead:

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm pack
dsh plugin --profile headless add "file:$PWD/$(ls -t dsh-biorxiv-*.tgz | head -1)"
```

Verify:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile headless list
dsh --profile headless "Use biorxiv_search to search for 'protein language model' and report the first title and DOI."
```

`dsh plugin add` is a pnpm forwarder: a `--profile` is required, and `pnpm` must be on `PATH`.

## CLI

```bash
dsh-biorxiv search "protein language model" --limit 5
dsh-biorxiv paper 10.64898/2026.07.21.739963
dsh-biorxiv latest --days 2 --limit 10
dsh-biorxiv export "hippocampal ripple" --format markdown --out refs.md
dsh-biorxiv digest "protein language model" --limit 5
```

Each command prints one JSON envelope and exits `0` on success, `1` on a tool error, `2` on a usage error.

## MCP

Run the stdio server:

```bash
dsh-biorxiv-mcp
```

MCP client config example:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "biorxiv": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "--package", "dsh-biorxiv", "dsh-biorxiv-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

An npm package is not published yet. The `npx` form above works after publication; for a GitHub install, point the client at `node ~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/node_modules/dsh-biorxiv/dist/apps/mcp/main.js`.

The server exposes `biorxiv_search`, `biorxiv_paper`, `biorxiv_latest`, `biorxiv_export` and `biorxiv_digest` with the same JSON envelope.

## Configuration

Defaults live in the plugin schema; no config is required.

```json
{
  "cachePath": "~/.cache/dsh-biorxiv/cache.db",
  "cacheMode": "auto",
  "timeoutMs": 10000,
  "retries": 2,
  "maxBytes": 2000000,
  "userAgent": "dsh-biorxiv/0.1 (DeepSeek Harness plugin)",
  "summaryEnabled": false,
  "summaryModel": "deepseek-chat",
  "summaryBaseUrl": "https://api.deepseek.com",
  "summaryApiKeyEnv": "DEEPSEEK_API_KEY"
}
```

- `summaryEnabled`: default `false`. When true, `digest --summary` sends only public title/abstract to the configured model and labels output as machine-generated.
- The API key is read from the named environment variable; it is never written to config, cache or logs.
- CLI: `dsh-biorxiv digest "topic" --summary` opts in; it also enables the provider for that process.
- MCP: set `DSH_BIORXIV_SUMMARY=1` in the server environment, then call `biorxiv_digest` with `summary: true`.

- `cacheMode`: `auto` (SQLite when available, JSON fallback), `sqlite`, or `json`.
- Cache keys are SHA-256 hashes; query text is not written into the cache key.
- Delete the cache file to reset; it is disposable.

## Data sources and boundaries

- Search: Europe PMC REST (`SRC:PPR` + `PUBLISHER:"bioRxiv"`).
- Latest/version details: bioRxiv public API.
- Journal/retraction enrichment: Crossref and OpenAlex; failures are non-blocking.
- No full-text PDF download, no scraping behind 403/paywalls, no writes to source sites.
- Do not use for clinical, medical or investment decisions. Preprints are not peer-reviewed.

## Development

```bash
pnpm test
pnpm coverage
```

The coverage ratchet is enforced by `scripts/coverage-ratchet.mjs`; line coverage must not fall below `.coverage-baseline.json`.

## License

MIT. See `LICENSE`. Privacy and data flow: see `PRIVACY.md`.

plugins.description: Deterministic financial-data and valuation plugin for DeepSeek Harness: six ratio groups, forecast ratios, DCF slots, comparable PS/PE, IRR — one unified schema.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-valuation-service

A deterministic financial-data and valuation plugin for **DeepSeek Harness**. It reads a workpaper layout of `01.json` / `02.json` / `04.json`, computes six ratio groups, forecast ratios, DCF input slots, comparable PS / PE and IRR, and writes one unified schema per project set.

It registers one agent tool, **`valuation_service`**. No AI inference, no invented numbers: anything missing is left blank and marked `missing` for a human or a downstream research step to fill.

## What it computes

| Block | Content |
|---|---|
| `ratios.historical` | profitability, solvency, efficiency, cash flow, valuation, growth |
| `ratios.forecast` | forecast-period profitability / growth / expense; BS- and CF-dependent ratios marked missing |
| `dcf` | full input slots (WACC, g, tax, EBIT, D&A, capex, ΔWC, net debt), outputs, missing list, hand-off anchors |
| `comparable` | PS and PE in parallel: trimmed mean, all-sample mean, 1-year mean, pre-money multiple, premium |
| `irr` | target / conservative / optimistic, closed-vs-open judgement, deviation |
| `assumption_diff` | material assumptions vs assumptions computed from actuals, field by field |
| `pending` / `gate` | unresolved conflicts and C2–C7 gate status when the workpapers carry them |

## Input layout

```text
<base>/
├── 项目A/
│   └── json/
│       ├── 01.json   # financial.raw (BS/IS/CF) + financial.ratios
│       ├── 02.json   # assumptions.forecast + assumptions.comparables + assumptions.valuation
│       └── 04.json   # validation.irr_recompute
└── 项目B/
    └── json/...
```

`--base` defaults to `$DSH_VALUATION_BASE` or `./数据底表`. Projects are discovered dynamically: every directory with all three JSON files is included. No project list is hard-coded.

`01.json` may use either `raw = {bs, is, cf}` or report-title sections (e.g. `"一、资产负债表 · 资产"`); both are normalized.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin add https://github.com/zirscard/dsh-valuation-service
```

Or from a local directory:

```bash
dsh plugin add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-valuation-service
```

Restart DSH; a new session gets the `valuation_service` tool.

## Tool usage

```json
{
  "base": "/path/to/数据底表",
  "projects": "项目A,项目B",
  "write": true
}
```

- `base` (string, optional): workpaper root; relative paths resolve against the session working directory.
- `projects` (string or array, optional): restrict to these project directory names.
- `write` (boolean, optional, default `false`): write `<base>/valuations-service.json`.
- `out` (string, optional): override the output path.

The tool returns a per-project summary (DCF status and missing list, PS/PE status, IRR closed flag, assumption-diff count, gate) plus the output path.

## CLI usage

The Python entry point is usable without DSH (standard library only):

```bash
python3 core/valuation_service.py --base /path/to/数据底表 --dry-run
python3 core/valuation_service.py --base /path/to/数据底表 --projects 项目A
python3 core/valuation_service.py --base /path/to/数据底表 --write
python3 core/valuation_service.py --base /path/to/数据底表 --write --json
```

`--json` prints one machine-readable summary object; `--write` writes the aggregate file; without `--write` it is a dry run.

## Unified schema

```json
{
  "schema": "m1.valuation-service/v2",
  "project_id": "...",
  "project_name": "...",
  "currency": "CNY",
  "method": "...",
  "financial_inputs": {"period": "...", "is": {}, "bs": {}, "cf": {}},
  "ratios": {"historical": {}, "forecast": {}},
  "dcf": {"status": "computed|partial|unavailable", "inputs": {}, "outputs": {}, "missing": [], "m3_handoff": {}},
  "comparable": {"ps": {}, "pe": {}},
  "irr": {"target": null, "conservative": null, "optimistic": null, "closed": false, "judge": "", "dev": null},
  "assumption_diff": [],
  "pending": [],
  "gate": {}
}
```

The aggregate file wraps records as `{"schema": "m1.valuation-service/aggregate/v2", "generated_at": "...", "base": "...", "projects": [...], "errors": [...]}`.

## Formulas

- Ratios: gross / operating / net margin, ROE, ROA; current / quick / cash ratio, debt-to-equity, debt-to-assets, interest coverage; asset / inventory / receivables turnover and days; OCF ratios; PS / PE / EV / EV-EBITDA; revenue and net-income growth.
- DCF: `FCFF = EBIT × (1 − t) + D&A − capex − ΔWC`; `TV = FCFF_last × (1 + g) / (WACC − g)`; `EV = Σ PV(FCFF) + PV(TV)`; `equity = EV − net debt`.
- Comparable: trimmed mean (10% each side when n ≥ 5), all-sample mean, 1-year mean, pre-money multiple, premium.
- IRR: `(exit value / invested capital) ^ (1 / years) − 1`.
- Assumption diff: material assumption vs module-computed actual, per field.

Ratio formulas are adapted from [anthropics/claude-cookbooks · analyzing-financial-statements/calculate_ratios.py](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-cookbooks/blob/main/skills/custom_skills/analyzing-financial-statements/calculate_ratios.py) (MIT), mapped onto Chinese three-statement labels.

## Adaptation layer

Data variants are handled in one place instead of per project:

| Variant | Function | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| raw layout (`{bs,is,cf}` vs report-title sections) | `_normalize_raw` | normalize by 资产负债表 / 利润表 / 现金流量表 keywords |
| units (thousand / ten-thousand / million CNY) | `_unit_for` | field-name suffix first, then `forecast.unit` |
| field-name variants | `_find_param` | keyword match + exclusion words |
| total vs line item (`资产总计` vs `流动资产合计`) | `_find_val` | totals require an exact match, no substring fallback |
| self-comparison in the comp set | `_included` | drop rows whose `treatment` says 自比 / 剔除 |
| no market PE multiple | `comparable.pe.status=assumption` | use the assumption range explicitly, never present it as a market multiple |

If a new variant is structural (layout / unit / naming), add it to the adapter. If it is a measurement convention, add it to the skill formulas. If data is missing, leave it blank and mark `missing`.

## DCF hand-off

Missing DCF inputs stay blank; `dcf.m3_handoff.anchors` lists what each one needs:

| Missing input | Anchor to fill |
|---|---|
| WACC | risk-free rate / beta / equity risk premium / capital structure |
| g | long-run GDP growth / industry terminal growth |
| capex | capex plan / construction in progress / capacity expansion |
| D&A | depreciation and amortization policy |
| ΔWC | receivables / inventory / payables turnover forecast |
| tax rate | effective tax rate |
| net debt | interest-bearing debt − cash |

## Test

```bash
python3 test/run_tests.py
```

The test builds a synthetic three-project workpaper set in a temporary directory (no client data), runs the service, and checks ratio values, DCF missing slots, comparable status, IRR and the written aggregate file.

## Boundaries

- No AI inference, no model calls, no network requests.
- No client data or project names are shipped in this repository.
- Missing inputs are marked, not fabricated.
- It does not replace a valuation model: it standardizes inputs and keeps the slots.

## License

MIT. Ratio formulas adapted from anthropics/claude-cookbooks (MIT); see [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](./THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

bilibili-note 的 DSH 插件封装版（衍生自 3588834014-del/bilibili-note）：把 B站视频链接变成 Obsidian 结构化笔记，只拉字幕不下载视频。
plugins.readme_text:
# bilibili-note

> **DSH plugin packaging of [`3588834014-del/bilibili-note`](https://github.com/3588834014-del/bilibili-note).**
>
> This repository is the **plugin edition**: the upstream project plus a DeepSeek Harness
> bundle wrapper (`package.json` / `cordis.patch.yml` / `lib/index.js`). The original
> skill + CLI lives upstream — use that one if you don't need to install it as a dsh plugin.
> GitHub does not allow forking a repository into the same account, so this is a derivative
> copy rather than a fork-network fork.

> **Turn Bilibili videos into structured Obsidian notes — subtitles only, never the video.**
>
> 中文说明见 [README.zh-CN.md](README.zh-CN.md)。

[![CI](https://github.com/3588834014-del/bilibili-note/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/3588834014-del/bilibili-note/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Python 3.8+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.8%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/)

A small CLI — plus an optional agent skill — that turns a Bilibili video into a structured
Markdown note in your Obsidian vault. It downloads **only the subtitle file** (`--skip-download`),
cleans the timestamps, and writes a note with YAML front matter, a summary section, bullet
points carrying clickable `?t=` jump links, and the full transcript collapsed at the bottom.

The repetitive half (fetch, parse, format, verify) is a script. The judgment half (summary,
key points, tags) is left as a documented contract you or an agent fill in.

```
Bilibili URL ──▶ fetch ──▶ manifest.json ──▶ [you / agent] ──▶ content.json ──▶ write ──▶ note.md
                  │         subtitles +                      summary, bullets,       │
                  │         timestamped segments             tags                    │
                  └── yt-dlp, subtitles only ────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Real output

`fetch` on a real video — note what is *not* there: no `.mp4`, `.flv`, `.m4a` or `.part`,
only the subtitle file and its manifest.

![fetch: subtitles only, no media files](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/3588834014-del/bilibili-note/main/docs/images/demo-fetch.png)

And the note it produces (Obsidian rendering — front matter, clickable `?t=` jump links,
summary, bullets, tags). Screenshot taken from a real run, not a mock-up:

![the generated note](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/3588834014-del/bilibili-note/main/docs/images/demo-note.png)

## Why this one

- **Subtitles only.** `--skip-download` is mandatory, and the tool verifies no media file
  (`.mp4/.flv/.m4a/.part`) landed in the working directory. No reverse-engineering, no
  private APIs — just `yt-dlp`.
- **Multi-part videos are merged.** For an anthology (B站 分P 合集) it fetches every part's
  subtitles and rebases the timestamps onto one continuous timeline. Verified on a real
  6-part anthology: **2:10:32 → 2807 segments / 33214 characters**, matching an independent
  concatenation segment-for-segment. A part with no subtitles is skipped **while keeping its
  time slot**, so later timestamps stay correct.
- **It refuses to produce garbage.** If two parts yield byte-identical subtitles, it errors out
  instead of silently emitting a note whose content is one part repeated N times. (That exact
  bug shipped during development and was caught by this guard.)
- **No subtitles? It skips and tells you.** It never fabricates content or writes an empty note.

## Install

No dependencies — standard library only. `yt-dlp` is an **external command**, not a Python package.

### As a DSH plugin (recommended for DeepSeek Harness)

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:3588834014-del/bilibili-note-plugin
```

This is a **bundle plugin** that registers the `bilibili-note` skill straight into the DSH skill
catalog — no manual copying into `~/.agents/skills`. Restart your profile afterwards and the
skill is available; the model picks it up from phrases like 「B站笔记」 or a pasted BV link.

The plugin ships its own copy of `scripts/bili_note.py`, `docs/` and `SKILL.md`, and rewrites
the `<skill-dir>` placeholders in the skill body to the **absolute install path**, so the model
never has to guess where the script lives. Uninstall with
`dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-bilibili-note`.

> There is no npm package yet, so this plugin is **source-installed** — it is listed on
> [dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org) but will not appear in the in-app plugin store.
> pnpm ≥10 may ask you to allow the git dependency's build script; this package has no
> `prepare` script, so nothing runs at install time.

### As a standalone CLI

```bash
pipx install git+https://github.com/3588834014-del/bilibili-note.git
# or
git clone https://github.com/3588834014-del/bilibili-note.git
cd bilibili-note && python -m pip install .
```

Then:

```bash
bili-note --version
bili-note note "https://www.bilibili.com/video/BVxxxxxxxxx" \
    --note-dir ~/MyVault/Sources/Videos
```

### As a plain agent skill (no plugin)

```bash
python scripts/install.py            # installs to ~/.agents/skills/bilibili-note
python scripts/install.py --dry-run  # show what would be copied
```

The skill then appears in the dsh skill catalog and can be triggered with phrases like
「B站笔记」. The plugin, the skill-file install and the CLI all share the same implementation
(`scripts/bili_note.py`).

### Requirements

| Requirement | Notes |
|---|---|
| Python 3.8+ | stdlib only |
| [`yt-dlp`](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp) | `pip install -U yt-dlp` — the **only** download channel |
| Bilibili login cookies | Required for AI subtitles; see below |
| DSH `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0` | Only for the plugin/skill route |

### Permissions and external services

Worth knowing before you install, since this tool touches the network and your vault:

- **Network**: talks to `bilibili.com` through `yt-dlp` only. It downloads **subtitles**, never
  video or audio (`--skip-download` is mandatory and verified).
- **Credentials**: reads a Bilibili cookie file from `$BILI_COOKIES` or `./cookies.txt`. It
  writes a **normalized temporary copy** next to the work dir for yt-dlp; it never uploads,
  logs, or commits cookies.
- **Filesystem**: writes notes into the `--note-dir` you pass, plus a scratch work directory.
  Nothing outside those two paths is modified.
- **No telemetry, no extra dependencies**, no reverse-engineered APIs.

## Cookies (required)

Bilibili's AI-subtitle endpoint needs an authenticated session.

1. Install the **Get cookies.txt LOCALLY** browser extension.
2. Log into [bilibili.com](https://www.bilibili.com).
3. Export `cookies.txt`.
4. Put it in your working directory, or point at it:

```bash
export BILI_COOKIES=/path/to/cookies.txt      # Linux / macOS
$env:BILI_COOKIES = "C:\path\cookies.txt"     # PowerShell
```

Videos where the uploader supplied their own subtitles may work without this.

### ⚠️ Why you can't feed the export straight to yt-dlp

This is the single most surprising thing in this repository. That extension writes lines like:

```
.bilibili.com	FALSE	/	FALSE	1819635894	SESSDATA	xxxxx
```

The domain carries a leading dot, yet the host-only flag in column 2 is `FALSE`. Python's
`http.cookiejar` asserts:

```python
assert domain_specified == initial_dot
```

The mismatch raises, and yt-dlp refuses to load the **entire file**:

```
ERROR: invalid Netscape format cookies file '...': '.bilibili.com\tFALSE\t/...'
```

The practical symptom is nasty: subtitles never arrive, and the error looks like
*"this video has no subtitles."* The fix is normalization — strip the leading dot and set the
flag to `FALSE` (a host-only cookie is still sent to `api.bilibili.com` and friends, so the
session is preserved). `normalize_cookies()` does this, plus filters to the `bilibili` domain
and de-duplicates by `domain/path/name`. You never have to do it by hand.

## Output directory

Nothing is hard-coded. Pick either:

```bash
bili-note note "<URL>" --note-dir "<vault>/Sources/Videos"    # explicit

export BILI_VAULT="/path/to/MyVault"                           # or environment
export BILI_TARGET_DIR="Sources/Videos"

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-shutdown-idle

DSH 插件：**开启后，等所有会话都结束（没有任何 Agent 在跑）并保持空闲，自动执行关机**（也可选重启 / 休眠 / 睡眠 / 锁定 / 注销）。

## 用起来

1. 打开「设置 → 会话结束后关机」，点 **开启**。
2. 正常派活给任意会话；所有会话的回合结束后，插件先等 `空闲确认` 秒，再进入 `倒计时` 秒。
3. 倒计时结束即执行所选动作。期间任何会话重新开始运行，或点界面上的 **取消**，这次动作都会被撤销。

右上角（浮层右下角）在开启后会常驻一张小卡片，显示当前阶段与剩余秒数，并带「取消」按钮。**按住卡片标题即可拖动**：松手后位置写进浏览器 `localStorage`（键 `dsh.shutdown-idle.pill.position`），下次打开停在原处；拖动过程始终夹在视口内（留 8px 可见），窗口变小也会自动收回视野。从「取消」按钮上按下不会误触发拖动。

## 判据

- **会话进行中** = `ctx.get('agents').list()` 里存在 `status === 'running'` 的 Agent（与 dshmarket 的更新守卫同一判据）。这一条固定生效，不可关闭。
- **后台任务** = `ctx.get('jobs')` 中 `status === 'running'` 的作业（含各存活会话名下的作业），即 DSH 界面里的「后台任务」；由配置项 `considerJobs` 决定是否检测，关掉后完全不再统计。
- 拿不到 `agents` 服务时按 **不空闲** 处理：宁可不执行，也不误关机。
- 「必须观察到会话运行过」默认开启：刚开启且没有任何任务时不会执行动作。

## 参数

| 参数 | 默认 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 动作 | `shutdown` | `shutdown` / `restart` / `hibernate` / `sleep` / `lock` / `logoff` / `none`（`none` = 只记录不执行） |
| 空闲确认 | 20 秒 | 全部空闲后先确认这么久，避免回合间隙被误判为结束 |
| 倒计时 | 60 秒 | 可取消的执行前倒计时 |
| 必须观察到会话运行过 | 是 | 防止刚开启就执行 |
| 后台任务也算占用（`considerJobs`） | 是 | 关掉后完全不再检测后台任务（shell 作业） |

设置页把这几项收在「什么算『还在忙』」区块里：会话在跑固定算忙，下面两个复选框是配置项。

初始值来自本包 `cordis.patch.yml` 的行 `config`；界面改动写入 `<DSH_HOME>/dsh-shutdown-idle/settings.json` 并优先生效（删除该文件即回落到 patch 初始值）。

**开关状态不持久化**：宿主重启后一律是「关闭」，避免开机即误关机。

## 接口

| 方法 | 路径 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/dsh-shutdown/api/state` | 开关、阶段、倒计时、运行中会话/作业 |
| POST | `/dsh-shutdown/api/config` | `{ enabled?, action?, settleSeconds?, countdownSeconds?, requireActivity?, considerJobs? }` |
| POST | `/dsh-shutdown/api/cancel` | 取消倒计时并关闭开关 |
| GET | `/dsh-shutdown` | 客户端半不可用时的兜底页面 |

## 平台

动作命令是 Windows 自带的 `shutdown` / `rundll32`。非 Windows 平台上，除 `none` 外的动作会被降级为 `none` 并在界面标注，不会执行命令。

## 字段一览

- `host.v2.mjs` — Host 半：状态机、HTTP 接口、命令派发、兜底页面。（`host.v1.mjs` 为上一版，保留以便回滚。）
- `client.js` — 浏览器半：设置页分区 + `shell.overlay` 浮层卡片（可拖动，`useDraggable` 负责指针捕获、边界夹取与位置持久化）。
- `cordis.patch.yml` — bundle 补丁：插入插件行与初始配置。

升级宿主半代码时换文件名（`host.v1.mjs` → `host.v2.mjs`）并同步 `package.json` 的 `main` / `exports`：config-only 热重载不会重新加载同一路径的模块。

# dshx-skill-manager

> A Settings page that lists every installed skill with an on/off switch and a short AI-generated summary.

在 **设置 → 技能管理** 里列出 DSH 当前解析到的所有技能（用户级、项目级），每个技能一个开关，并附一句简短的中文概述。

- **开关**：插件在自身生命周期内包装技能注册表的 `snapshot()` / `get()`，停用的技能对模型目录、`skill` 工具和 `/skill` 命令都不可见。技能文件不会被修改，卸载插件即完全还原。
- **概述**：可用默认模型批量生成（带缓存，描述变化才重新生成）；没有 AI 概述时用描述的第一句。

## 配置（`cordis.patch.yml`）

| 字段 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `summarize` | `true` | 是否用默认模型生成概述 |
| `summaryMaxChars` | `60` | 概述长度上限 |
| `stateFile` | 空 | 状态文件，默认 `$DSH_HOME/dshx-skill-manager/state.json` |

## 安装

```sh
# Web profile
dsh plugin --profile web add github:callaumyan-design/dshx-skill-manager
# Desktop（用 DSH Desktop 自带的 dsh 命令，先从托盘完全退出 Desktop）
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:callaumyan-design/dshx-skill-manager
```

安装后重启 DSH。卸载：`dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove dshx-skill-manager`。

## 兼容性

在 DeepSeek Harness 0.2.0-rc.2（desktop / web profile）上开发和使用。纯 JavaScript，无构建步骤，无安装脚本。

MIT

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin - persistent four-layer cognitive memory for agents, backed by vecRecall
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-vecrecall

> **A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that gives your agent persistent, four-layer cognitive memory.**

The plugin mounts six `vecrecall_*` tools onto the harness tool registry, backed by
[vecRecall](https://github.com/snowfoxHQ/vecRecall) — a local-first, four-layer cognitive memory
engine (L0 identity / L1 key moments / L2 semantic / L3 deep retrieval) with hybrid retrieval,
meaning-level deduplication, and everything stored on your own disk.

Memory work happens in a **long-lived Python process** that holds the embedding model, so repeated
tool calls cost milliseconds instead of reloading weights every time.

## Install

```bash
# 1. Python side (vecRecall runtime). There is no PyPI package yet, so install from GitHub:
pip install "vecrecall @ git+https://github.com/snowfoxHQ/vecRecall.git"

# 2. Mount the plugin into a dsh profile
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-vecrecall
```

Then restart that profile. The tools appear as `vecrecall_*`.

## Tools

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `vecrecall_remember` | Store a durable fact. Meaning-level dedup: near-duplicates merge instead of piling up. |
| `vecrecall_recall` | Pure semantic search. No results means a genuine miss — that is signal, not failure. |
| `vecrecall_context` | Build the four-layer bundle (L0/L1/L2/L3). Use at session start or when resuming a topic. |
| `vecrecall_list` | Structural listing by wing/topic. Also how you find an id to delete. |
| `vecrecall_forget` | Delete one memory by id or an unambiguous prefix. |
| `vecrecall_stats` | Store size and backend health. Cheap sanity check. |

Rules worth keeping in mind: `content` is stored **verbatim**, so write self-contained statements;
`summary` is display-only and never searched. Do not dump whole files or transient tool output into
memory.

## Configuration

Every field below has a working default; override only what you need in `cordis.yml`:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: vecrecall
      name: 'dsh-vecrecall'
      config:
        dataDir: '~/.vecrecall'      # where memories live, created on first start
        wing: 'default'              # namespace: a project, user, or domain
        embedder: 'auto'             # auto | bow | sentence | ollama | api
        python: 'python'             # interpreter used for the helper process
        chain: false                 # hash chain; ~2x storage, for tamper auditing
        startupTimeoutMs: 120000     # first start loads the embedding model
        toolTimeoutMs: 120000
        maxRenderChars: 8000         # cap rendered output to protect the context window
        onSensitive: redact       # redact | reject | allow; see "Credentials" below
```

`embedder: 'bow'` needs nothing extra and works fully offline; `'auto'` picks sentence-transformers
when installed and silently falls back to bag-of-words otherwise.

## Security

The helper service listens on `127.0.0.1` only and requires a random per-process bearer token. It is
never exposed on a network interface. Your memory store is plain files under `dataDir`.

### Credentials

Memories are stored as plain text, and retrieval requires embedding the plain text — so once a
secret lands in the store there is no way to recover. Encrypting it would mean giving up search.
The only reliable moment to act is before the write, so content is screened first:

| `onSensitive` | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `redact` (default) | Replaces credential parts with `***`, keeps the rest |
| `reject` | Refuses the write and tells the model to strip the secret |
| `allow` | Stores content as-is (not recommended) |

Redaction preserves the retrievable meaning: `postgres://app:s3cret@db.internal:5432/hestia` is
stored as `postgres://app:***@db.internal:5432/hestia`, so "which host is the database on" still
recalls, while the password never touches disk.

This is pattern matching, not a mathematical guarantee — it will not catch a bare password with no
keyword context. The durable fix is upstream: keep credentials in env vars or a vault, and let the
agent reference only the variable name (`DB_URL`). The same guard runs inside the vecRecall engine,
so CLI and skill writes are covered too.

## Compatibility

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Verified against | `@deepseek-ai/cordis` 4.0.5, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` 0.0.1-rc.1 |
| Type check | `npm run check` passes (strict, erasable-syntax-only) |
| Runtime | Python bridge smoke-tested end to end: cold start ~23s, then 20–120ms per call |
| Live harness run | verified on DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 (desktop app): tools registered, memory written and read back |

## Troubleshooting

**`vecRecall 调用失败：vecRecall 未安装或不可导入`** — the interpreter the plugin launches cannot
`import vecrecall`. If you installed into a virtualenv, point `python` at it:

```yaml
config:
  python: '/path/to/venv/bin/python'
```

**First tool call is slow** — expected: that call loads the embedding model. Everything after it is
fast, because the process stays alive for the lifetime of the plugin. Raise `startupTimeoutMs` if
your machine takes longer than 120s.

**Recalls back almost nothing** — you are likely on the bag-of-words fallback. Install
`sentence-transformers` and start numpy-based search, or set `embedder: 'sentence'`.

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm run check     # tsc --noEmit
```

`src/bridge.ts` owns the Python process, `src/tools.ts` declares the tools, `src/index.ts` is the
plugin entry (`apply(ctx)`).

Uses only erasable TypeScript so a plain `node` with type stripping can load it.
